title: Low Water Pressure? Check the Aerator First
description: When low water pressure affects only one sink, the problem is usually a physical blockage at the fixture rather than a main supply issue. Faucet aerators contain small wire or plastic mesh screens designed to shape the water stream and reduce splashing. Over time, rust flakes, sediment, and mineral scale accumulate inside this mesh, restricting water flow. Before assuming you have clogged supply lines or a failing pressure-reducing valve, unscrew the aerator at the tip of the spout. Clean out trapped debris with vinegar and a brush, or replace the screen assembly. Is your low pressure isolated to one fixture or across your entire home?

The viewer immediately notices the physical debris blocking the water outlet point. This visual directly links localized low pressure at a single fixture to a simple, easily inspected component.

on_image_text.hook: Low Pressure at Just One Faucet?
on_image_text.explanation: Sediment and mineral scale collect inside the fine mesh screen of the faucet aerator, severely restricting water flow.
on_image_text.takeaway: Unscrew and clean the aerator screen before replacing supply lines or valves.
